direction: Long-only spot rotation from the BTC/ETH relative-price-ratio z-score
hypothesis: Large deviations in log(BTC/ETH) from their trailing mean may partially revert; buying the relatively lagging asset and exiting as the ratio normalizes could diversify momentum approaches. Crypto relative relationships may be non-stationary, so sensitivity across lookback and entry threshold is mandatory.
rule: For each completed UTC daily decision j=i-1, calculate x_j=ln(close_BTC[j]/close_ETH[j]). Calculate reference mean and sample standard deviation from the prior L completed ratio observations x[j-L:j] (current x_j excluded). z_j=(x_j-reference_mean)/reference_std; if std is zero, set z=0. If flat and z>entry_threshold, target ETH (BTC relatively rich); if z<-entry_threshold, target BTC (ETH relatively rich); otherwise stay cash. If holding ETH, remain while z>0.5, exit to cash when z<=0.5, and switch to BTC when z<-entry_threshold. If holding BTC, remain while z<-0.5, exit to cash when z>=-0.5, and switch to ETH when z>entry_threshold. Entry tests take precedence over exit-to-cash at opposite extremes; values at the entry boundary do not enter, and values at the exit boundary exit. Trade only when target changes. Execute after the daily signal at next UTC day 00:01 one-minute open. A switch sells first, then buys with remaining cash at the same recorded timestamp. Failed sells preserve the current holding and suppress the new buy; failed buys remain cash and are reconsidered next daily decision. No shorting, leverage, simultaneous positions, interest, cross-account transfer, timed exit, or pre-OOS fills.
allocation: Each parameter configuration is a separate $2,000 USDT unlevered spot account. At most 100% is held in one coin; otherwise the account is in USDT. This is a state-dependent long-only allocation, not a fixed BTC/ETH weight portfolio.

failure_gates.interpretation: Passing means this repeated-history screen only; it does not establish an independent holdout or stable live profits.

literature.citation: Mallik, S. (2021). Pricing cryptocurrencies: Modelling the ETHBTC spot-quotient variation as a diffusion process. arXiv:2111.11609.
literature.use: The paper reports mean reversion in intraday deviations between Binance ETHBTC and ETHUSDT/BTCUSDT quotient series. This daily log-price-ratio rotation is a simpler long-only adaptation, not a replication; ratio mean reversion in this two-year reused sample is not assumed.

data.source: Binance spot 1m OHLCV, normalized closed bars
data.reuse_disclosure: This period has been repeatedly used for strategy development and validation; it is not an untouched final holdout.

walk_forward.parameter_fit: None; all parameters frozen before evaluation. Daily ratio and trailing reference moments use only completed closes. No OOS position is replayed from warm-up history; portfolio state carries continuously over all adjacent test folds.

execution.reference_price: Next UTC day 00:01 one-minute open, after the previous daily candle close is available. Switches liquidate the current coin before buying the other at the same timestamp; both legs are costed. Historic L2 quotes are unavailable, so half-spread and impact are estimates, not fill guarantees.

costs.impact_formula: 0.5 * sample std(previous 20 complete UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order budget / mean quote turnover(previous 20 complete UTC days))

prior_evidence.finding: All 16 initial registry rows have actual backtest/report evidence; no exact missing-result starting configuration to rerun.
